sources.entry: Nimbus - Modern drag-and-drop homelab dashboard with visual editor and simple configuration. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Nimbus is a self-hosted, Docker-deployed homelab dashboard for monitoring service health and organizing apps with drag-and-drop tiles, multi-user accounts, and themes.
summary.what_it_does: Nimbus provides a web dashboard for listing and monitoring homelab services, with real-time health checks, response time tracking, and status history with uptime graphs. It supports local JWT accounts and OAuth2 sign-in (Google, GitHub, Discord), role-based access control, and an admin panel for user management. Users can customize their view with per-user wallpapers, light/dark mode, accent colors, a canvas layout, and drag-and-drop service tiles, plus search via / or Ctrl+K. It exports Prometheus metrics and has configurable check intervals. The README describes a 2.0 dev-image widget system (clock, notes, weather, RSS, Docker containers, etc.) and integrations showing live numbers from apps such as Pi-hole, Jellyfin and Home Assistant, with credentials encrypted using an ENCRYPTION_KEY.
use_cases: organize self-hosted apps on a dashboard
export service health metrics to Prometheus
show live stats from Pi-hole or Jellyfin on tiles
deploy a homelab dashboard with Docker
how_to_run: Create docker-compose.yml with the nimbus and nimbus-postgres (db) services from the README
Open the browser on port 3000 and create the first account
For production, set DB_PASSWORD and JWT_SECRET in a .env file
notable: Zero-config Docker deployment with auto-generated secrets on first run
Smart self-signed certificate handling for health checks
Integrations with live numbers on service tiles, with encrypted credentials
Hosted Nimbus Cloud option alongside the free self-hosted version
Multi-tier image tags: latest, pinned versions, beta, and dev
caveats: Widgets and many integrations are on the dev image and listed as planned, not yet available in stable releases
Separate nimbus-backend and nimbus-frontend images no longer receive updates; migration is required
Going back from dev or beta to latest on the same database is not supported
keywords: see if my services are down
